The final terms …

• Cowboys get: CB Joey Porter Jr.

• Steelers get: 2027 sixth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick.

Interestingly enough, the sixth-rounder is the Steelers’ pick that Dallas got as part of the Pickens trade. Porter is going to Dallas without a new contract.

When the Steelers listed “conditioning” and “not injury-related” along with the back issue that Joey Porter Jr. reported as part of his injury-report designation, this thing was probably over. That’s essentially publicly calling the player on it.

Obviously, money is at the root of the trade. But having a contract dispute and needing to trade a good player away off a team built to win right now are two different things. Pittsburgh went from the first place to the second place with Porter, and here we are.

Once Joey Porter Jr. enters the lineup, four of the Cowboys’ 11 defensive starters will be vets who arrived via trade since last August—Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams, Rashan Gary and Porter. With Micah Parsons and Osa Odifhizuwa out via trade.
